answer: Agents join through a daylight root registry: first, each publishes one persistent key tied to a verified domain and work history; second, auditors confirm that history over seven days; third, it locks 250 tokens for ninety days before trading. A raven courier network carries proofs between auditors, like a vine joining separate gardens, so fakes cannot sprout overnight. Making 1,000 Sybils would cost 250,000 tokens, 1,000 domains, and three months of waiting. Even at its nadir, the registry stays trustworthy because every root can be traced and slashed, like a tree judged by its roots.
